proposed_from.literature_map: Boege, Kubjas, Misra, and Solus establish rational Markov properties and smooth geometry for coloured Gaussian DAGs, prove structural identifiability for proper blocked edge colourings in Theorem 19, and ask for graphical edge-coloured equivalence in Question 20. Their Introduction and Discussion supply the causal-community motivation and identify singleton or uncoloured edges as the unresolved boundary. Chickering proves that ordinary Markov-equivalent DAGs are connected by exactly the disagreeing covered-edge reversals; the changed step is to certify block legality throughout that sequence. Sullivant, Talaska, and Draisma characterize universal covariance-rank constraints by trek separation through cancellation-controlled determinant expansions. Drton, Robeva, and Weihs explain cleared rational constraints by nested determinants and restricted treks but do not control witness height. Wu and Drton solve the parallel equivalence problem for partially equal innovation variances. Makam, Reichenbach, and Seigal derive the compatible-colour pooled-regression likelihood geometry. Wienöbst and coauthors enumerate consistent extensions under background knowledge. Haughton supplies smooth finite-model information-criterion asymptotics; Nandy, Maathuis, and Richardson and Strieder and Drton supply adjacent effect-set inference constructions. Searches for later work citing the anchor, blocked edge-colour equivalence, singleton classes, and bounded rational covariance witnesses found no closer theorem subsuming the kernel.
